name: cside first-party application-to-verification case

attribution.legal_posture: First-party employer account of cside's experience. The DPRK characterization is speaker-reported; court finding, government attribution, and legal-identity determination regarding any candidate are outside the account.

ttps: Escalate projected-document or workflow anomalies for independent human verification
Review application, assessment-integrity, interview-coherence, identity-verification, and browser/device evidence cumulatively
Use job-relevant and consistently applied controls rather than demographic, nationality, accent, appearance, or other protected-characteristic proxies
caveats: Controls should be documented, proportionate, job-relevant, consistently applied, accessible to candidates with disabilities, and subject to human review and an appeal or correction path where feasible.

Individual signals such as latency, VPN use, virtual machines, typing patterns, assessment scores, or verification friction can have benign explanations; each requires corroboration before attribution.
Nationality, ethnicity, accent, language, age, sex, disability, appearance, location, and other demographic or protected characteristics require evidence beyond the characteristic itself.
The recording covers candidate-risk tooling; product efficacy, false-positive rates, population prevalence, and universal applicant affiliation status are unmeasured.
This record preserves a named first-party employer/control case; worker, persona, stolen-identity victim and candidate profiles belong to separate records.

infrastructure.claim: The speaker describes a high-volume application funnel with polished work histories, active code-hosting profiles, and unusually high standardized assessment scores.

The speaker describes interview lag and an incoherent answer consistent with outside assistance, followed by an identity-verification escalation in which a live check reportedly detected a projected document even though operational pressure still resulted in approval.

The speaker reports browser-side and workflow observations including latency, VPN and virtual-machine indicators, unusual fonts, burst-like typing, standardized copied assessment answers, and increasingly automated browser completion.

Use multiple job-relevant workflow, device, browser, assessment-integrity, and verification signals for escalation and human review; do not treat any single signal as proof and do not use demographic traits or protected characteristics as proxies.

sources.support: First-party account by cside's founder of cside's own application, interview, identity-verification, and browser-observation workflow. The recording supports the cumulative workflow observations at the cited timestamps; DPRK attribution remains speaker-reported rather than judicially determined
